intent: Keep enough systemd journal on the Arch desktop to diagnose a failure two weeks later: raise the installed cap from 300M to 4G and only vacuum a journal that is actually past it.
scope: the three test suites that pin those values
changes: SystemMaxUse=300M -> 4G in the drop-in each script writes and in the already-configured check.
Vacuum threshold: usage must be reported in G with an integer part >= 4, instead of any value in G; vacuum target 4G.
Report: 'journal is large' only past 4G, so a 2G journal is deliberate retention, not a finding.

verification.evidence: journalctl --disk-usage: 305.1M in the file system; cap now 4G

risks: Up to 4G of /var/log/journal on a 3.6T disk with 1.8T free -- negligible.
Three copies of the same logic still exist; they were changed together but remain duplicates.
rollback: git revert the commit and re-run the fix script, or write SystemMaxUse=300M into the drop-in and restart systemd-journald.
